product_family: Colossyan Creator: AI avatar video generator for corporate training and enablement (video creation, courses, localization, delivery, analytics), with self-serve Free/Starter/Business tiers and a separate Enterprise tier (SSO, custom avatars, multi-workspace, SCORM export).

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II
certifications.proof_quote: Colossyan holds SOC 2 Type II certification, independently audited by a third-party firm.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on Colossyan's own domain. The vendor's /security page references ISO 27001 only as a standard it requires of its own sub-processors and partner vendors, not as Colossyan's own certification. A third-party directory (Nudge Security) displays an 'ISO 27001 Compliant' badge with no supporting evidence or link.

certifications.name: GDPR (compliance posture, not a certification)
certifications.proof_quote: Colossyan complies with the EU General Data Protection Regulation... We process personal data lawfully, maintain data processing agreements (DPAs), and support data subject access requests.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: Customer warrants that it will not use the Services to store or transmit any 'protected health information' as defined by HIPAA (Enterprise Terms, Section 5.1); standard Terms Section 7.1(ix) similarly bars uploading PHI. No Business Associate Agreement (BAA) is offered in either Standard or Enterprise terms.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on Colossyan's own domain; Colossyan does not process cardholder payment data directly (billing is handled via third-party payment processors). A third-party directory (Nudge Security) shows a 'PCI Compliant' badge with no evidence or link.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on Colossyan's own domain. The vendor's security page references following 'the transparency and risk management principles of the EU AI Act' but does not claim ISO 42001 certification.

certifications.name: CSA STAR
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on Colossyan's own domain. A third-party directory (Nudge Security) shows a 'CSA STAR Level 1 Compliant' badge with no evidence or link.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on Colossyan's own domain; Colossyan is not a US federal government cloud offering. A third-party directory (Nudge Security) shows a 'FedRAMP Compliant' badge with no evidence or link.

privacy.ai_training_note: The vendor's security marketing page and privacy notice state that customer documents, scripts, and generated videos are never used to train Colossyan's AI models, and that third-party AI vendors are contractually prohibited from training on Colossyan input. The Enterprise Terms of Service (Section 4.2) carve out one exception: Colossyan may use a customer's own recordings to train the specific AI model that creates and operates that customer's Custom Created Avatar. This is a narrow, customer-specific use (building the customer's own avatar), not training Colossyan's general-purpose models on customer content; the exception is not mentioned on the marketing security page.
privacy.data_region: Infrastructure hosted on AWS in EU and US regions; Colossyan Inc. is a US entity with subsidiaries/registered offices in London (UK) and Budapest (Hungary); the general privacy notice separately states hosting occurs in Germany and the UK for EU/UK users, with data transfers outside the EEA relying on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs).

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: TLS 1.3 for all data transmitted between browser and Colossyan servers.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: AES-256 for customer data stored on Colossyan servers.

security.name: Hosting
security.value: AWS infrastructure in EU and US regions; 99.9% uptime SLA with 1-hour RTO/RPO cited on the security page.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Annual third-party penetration tests; reports available via the Trust Center under NDA.

security.name: Attack surface monitoring
security.value: Real-time monitoring via UpGuard, with a safety score cited as consistently above 900 (self-reported by the vendor).

security.name: Enterprise access controls
security.value: SAML and OIDC SSO, custom roles/permissions, multi-workspace architecture, available on the Enterprise tier.

security.name: Breach notification
security.value: Affected customers notified within GDPR-required timeframes (72 hours).

products.name: Colossyan Creator (Free / Starter / Business)
products.data_scope: Scripts, uploaded documents, generated videos, and any stock/custom avatar recordings the user uploads; standard Terms grant Colossyan broader internal research/service-improvement rights over Customer Materials than Enterprise terms do.
products.notes: Free plan (3 min/month, shared avatars), Starter ($19-27/mo), Business ($70-88/mo per editor) tiers; no SSO/SAML, no BAA, PHI upload prohibited under Section 7.1(ix) of standard Terms.

products.name: Colossyan Enterprise
products.data_scope: Same content types as self-serve, plus SSO-authenticated workspace data; PHI storage/transmission still explicitly prohibited (no BAA offered).
products.notes: Adds SAML/OIDC SSO, custom roles, multi-workspace isolation, SCORM export, custom quotes; only tier where Custom Created Avatar recordings may be used to train a customer-specific avatar model per Enterprise Terms Section 4.2.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium SaaS: Free, Starter (~$19-27/mo), Business (~$70-88/mo per editor), and custom-quoted Enterprise (SSO, SCORM, brand kits).
compare.data_residency: AWS-hosted in EU and US regions (with UK/Germany hosting cited separately for EU/UK privacy-notice purposes); no dedicated self-hosted or on-prem option found.

flags: The trust center at security.colossyan.com is a JS-rendered portal; the SOC 2 Type II claim is corroborated only via the vendor's own /security marketing page, not the trust center's detailed content.

A third-party directory (Nudge Security) displays generic 'compliant' badges for Colossyan covering SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, FedRAMP, and CSA STAR Level 1, with no supporting evidence or links. These badges contradict what Colossyan's own site and Terms say: HIPAA is explicitly disclaimed, and ISO 27001, PCI, FedRAMP, and CSA STAR are not mentioned anywhere on the vendor's own domain.

Marketing copy on the security page states customer content is 'never used to train our AI models,' but the Enterprise Terms of Service carve out an exception allowing use of a customer's own recordings to train that customer's Custom Created Avatar model.

Minor inconsistency between the security page (hosting described as AWS in EU/US regions) and the general privacy notice (hosting described as Germany and the UK for EU/UK users); likely reflects different infrastructure providers for different services rather than a real conflict, but not fully reconciled from public pages alone.
